title: Restaurant-Style Chicken Dum Biryani
description: An aromatic Hyderabadi-style dum biryani made with overnight-marinated chicken, CDS Special Biryani Masala, fragrant basmati rice, crispy fried onions, herbs, and slow dum cooking.

ingredients.item: orange food color or saffron milk

steps: Wash the basmati rice until the water runs clear and soak it for 30 minutes.

In a large bowl combine the chicken, yogurt, CDS Special Biryani Masala, Kashmiri chilli powder, turmeric, ginger-garlic paste, green chilies, lemon juice, fried onions, mint, cilantro, oil, and salt. Mix thoroughly until every piece is coated.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 8 hours, preferably overnight. A longer marinade produces more tender and flavorful chicken.
Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil. Add salt until the water tastes noticeably saltier than soup.
Add the bay leaves, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, and shahi jeera to the boiling water.
Cook the soaked rice until it is about 70% done. The grains should still have a firm center.
Immediately drain the rice and spread it on a tray for a minute to stop further cooking.
Grease a heavy-bottomed Dutch oven or handi with a little ghee.
Spread the marinated chicken evenly across the bottom of the pot.
Layer half of the rice over the chicken.
Sprinkle fried onions, cilantro, mint, and a few drops of kewra water and rose water.
Repeat with the remaining rice and garnish again with fried onions, herbs, ghee, and optional saffron milk or food color.
Seal the pot tightly with aluminum foil or dough and cover with the lid.
Cook over medium heat for 8-10 minutes until steam builds.
Reduce to the lowest heat (or place the pot on a tawa) and cook on dum for another 30-35 minutes.
Turn off the heat and let the biryani rest, unopened, for 15-20 minutes.
Open the lid gently and fluff the biryani from the sides using a flat spatula without breaking the rice.
Serve hot with raita, salan, sliced onions, and lemon wedges.
notes: Use aged long-grain basmati rice for separate, fluffy grains.
The rice should only be about 70% cooked before layering; it finishes cooking during dum.
The water used to boil the rice should taste very salty so the rice is seasoned internally.
Using the oil left from frying onions adds significant depth of flavor.
Do not skip the resting period after dum cooking; it allows the steam to redistribute evenly.
This recipe is designed to use the CDS Special Biryani Masala instead of commercial biryani masala.
For even more aroma, add a few drops of kewra water and rose water only in the final rice layer.
